verdict.oneLineSummary: Relatively straightforward OAuth flow; switch from Internal to Public integration to enable multi-tenant connects.

capabilityCheck.question: Can an agent create, read, and search Notion pages and databases?
capabilityCheck.detail: Notion's API supports full block-level and database read/write access. Note: Users must explicitly grant access to specific pages or parent databases when authorizing your integration.

prerequisites: A company domain and privacy policy URL for Public integrations

fields.name: Type
fields.note: Defaults to 'Internal'. You MUST switch to 'Public' under Distribution settings to allow any user to connect.

steps.text: Configure Capabilities under the Capabilities tab.

fields.name: Content Capabilities
fields.note: Read content, Update content, Insert content

fields.name: User Capabilities
fields.note: Read user information without email is usually sufficient

steps.text: Switch to 'Public' under Distribution and fill required metadata.

blockers.issue: New integrations are set to 'Internal' by default, meaning only your own workspace members can authenticate.
blockers.workaround: Navigate to the Distribution tab and toggle to 'Public Integration' to get the OAuth Client ID and Secret.

blockers.issue: Notion OAuth requires users to explicitly pick which root pages to share; if the user does not select a page, the agent receives 404 Not Found.
blockers.workaround: Display an instructional prompt in your onboarding UX telling users to select 'All Pages' or their target workspace root during Notion's consent dialog.

composio.recommendation: Composio provides fully managed Notion OAuth with standardized page and database action execution.

evidence.claim: Verified Notion integration setup: internal tokens are instant, while public distribution requires privacy URL and basic review.
evidence.label: SOURCED
